dct_description_sm: Yukon Government's (YG) climate change adaptation efforts began formally in 2009 with the inception of the Yukon Government Climate Change Action Plan and a clear articulation of adaptation as a key government priority. With the addition of Aboriginal Affairs and Northern Development Canada (AANDC), Northern Strategy Trust Fund, and other partnerships, YG was able to mobilize key adaptation projects across the territory. The overall intent was that effective climate change adaptation projects become mainstream activity for YG departments and the communities they affect thereby offering effective climate change adaptation approaches to all Yukoners. The Yukon Government chose several of Yukon's best proposals for adaptation projects and put them forth when applying for AANDC funding. This particular project aimed to examine the potential sensitivity of permafrost along the Alaska Highway, a vital overland supply route for several Yukon communities, to present and future climate variability. Specifically, this project focused on the northern 200 km of the Alaska Highway, from Destruction Bay to the Yukon/Alaska border. The communities of Destruction Bay, Burwash Landing and Beaver Creek, as well as the White River and Kluane First Nations, are situated adjacent to the highway, and are affected by changes to highway conditions as a result of permafrost degradation.
